recent_posts.title: We’ve stopped asking customers to bet on the right tool
recent_posts.summary: Swimm is pivoting from a SaaS tool to a services company, offering end-to-end legacy code modernization. The rationale: AI tool decisions have become a moving target, and enterprises need outcomes faster than procurement cycles allow. Swimm combines proprietary static analysis, LLMs, and senior engineers specializing in legacy systems to handle full modernization projects — discovery, planning, execution, and handoff. The shift is backed by market signals: OpenAI and Anthropic are launching enterprise services arms, and Sequoia data shows $6 in services spending for every $1 in AI product spend.

recent_posts.title: Swimm 2.0: the understanding platform for AI modernization
recent_posts.summary: Swimm 2.0 is announced as an 'understanding platform' targeting enterprise legacy application modernization. The core argument is that AI agents fail at modernization not due to code generation limitations, but because they cannot reliably understand complex legacy codebases — citing tests showing Claude Code achieved only 35% code coverage and 70% accuracy on a COBOL codebase with 42% variance between runs. Swimm 2.0 addresses this with deterministic static analysis that extracts business rules, decision logic, and data flows directly from source code, then uses AI only as a translation layer into business language. New features include business-domain navigation, Collections for governing modernization plans, source-traced business rules, an MCP server for AI agents to consume pre-validated context, and broad legacy language support including COBOL, CICS, and JCL. The platform claims up to 90% reduction in manual reverse engineering time, 75% time savings, and 61% cost reduction when agents use Swimm's context versus raw code.

recent_posts.title: Tests are the final gate: why comprehensive test coverage is how humans accept AI
recent_posts.summary: As AI agents take over more of software development, human review of individual code changes becomes impractical. The argument here is that comprehensive test suites must become the primary acceptance mechanism for AI-generated code. Tests serve as machine-executable specifications: they encode requirements from compliance documents, contracts, and institutional knowledge that AI cannot access from code alone. Most current test suites were built for regression detection, not for verifying organizational requirements, leaving a dangerous gap. The post examines the 'human-on-the-loop' shift, the circular problem of AI-generated tests, legacy migration challenges (COBOL, behavioral equivalence testing), and real-world failures from inadequate gates. The structural answer proposed is to inventory requirements before AI-assisted work begins and encode them as tests, rather than relying on code review at scale.

recent_posts.title: SwimmBench results show 75% faster and 61% cheaper Claude Code queries with pre-indexed context
recent_posts.summary: Swimm published benchmark results from SwimmBench, an internal tool measuring how pre-indexed code context affects Claude Code performance on a ~5M line C++ codebase (ScummVM). Testing compared Swimm's Deep Index (pre-computed code understanding) against Claude Code's native exploration. Results show 75% faster response times and 61% lower token costs when using indexed context, primarily because the AI skips file traversal and grep operations. The benchmark measures cost, latency, quality, and tool usage across architectural questions and explanation tasks. Swimm acknowledges limitations: internal testing with inherent bias, single codebase, and no external validation. The post targets engineering leaders evaluating AI tooling ROI at scale.

recent_posts.title: A blog article is not a product. No, Claude Code can’t understand COBOL applications.
recent_posts.summary: Swimm tested Claude Code (Opus 4.6) against its own deterministic platform on real CMS Medicare COBOL programs to evaluate business rule extraction quality. Results showed Claude covered only 24–35% of paragraphs on the larger program with up to 42% variance between identical runs, missed 27.5% of business rules entirely, dropped critical conditions (e.g., UNITS2 > 0), and hallucinated wrong regulatory dollar amounts. Swimm's deterministic static analysis achieved 100% coverage and accuracy on both programs. The post argues that LLM-based extraction is architecturally unsuited for mainframe modernization because it navigates code probabilistically rather than parsing the full AST, making it unreliable for regulated industries like healthcare and banking where every rule must be exact.

recent_posts.title: 7 application modernization trends reshaping enterprise IT in 2026
recent_posts.summary: Seven key trends are reshaping enterprise application modernization in 2026: AI readiness is driving modernization urgency as legacy systems lack the architecture for AI integration; AI-assisted tools are accelerating modernization workflows through hybrid deterministic and generative approaches; the skills gap continues worsening as mainframe experts retire without replacement; deep system understanding is recognized as foundational before any transformation; agentic AI represents new hype requiring careful evaluation; tighter budgets demand demonstrable ROI over experimental pilots; and leading organizations are adopting a "modernization factory" model treating modernization as ongoing capability rather than one-time projects. The common thread is organizations learning to separate practical execution from technology hype.

recent_posts.title: To trust an LLM, make lying harder than telling the truth
recent_posts.summary: Swimm's CTO shares lessons from building a semantic equivalence checker for AI-generated functional specs. Initial attempts using direct LLM comparison achieved 97% accuracy but failed on long specs where requirements were missed. Breaking down the task paradoxically worsened results to 46% accuracy, with the LLM hallucinating matches. The breakthrough came from forcing structured outputs: requiring specific evidence (matching IDs, quoted text) before conclusions, adding explicit verdict categories, and ordering the response to demand proof before judgment. This approach eliminated hallucinations by making lying harder than telling the truth, demonstrating that LLM reliability depends on designing response structures that require verifiable grounding.

recent_posts.title: Blackbox to blueprint: Extracting business logic from COBOL applications
recent_posts.summary: The process of extracting business logic from COBOL applications is crucial in modernizing legacy systems. It involves overcoming challenges such as scattered and intertwined logic, cryptic naming conventions, and technical environment complexity. The integration of static code analysis with modern AI techniques like LLMs can help in understanding COBOL code more effectively by providing context and resolving ambiguities. Incremental strategies are necessary to handle varying complexities in legacy codebases.

recent_posts.title: The hidden landmine in COBOL’s PERFORM statement: a control flow puzzle
recent_posts.summary: COBOL's PERFORM statement can lead to unexpected behavior in program control flow, especially when combined with GOTO statements. By creating a control block structure that resembles a stack, the language manages execution paths intricately. An example illustrates how COBOL's flow can be disrupted, demonstrating the challenge in accurately analyzing COBOL code due to hidden state persistence, impacting code parsing and understanding.
